purpose: Record two corrections the red team forced, one of them to a measurement I made myself, and the measured status of the O-3 premise.

CORRECTION_1_my_own_influence_probe_had_.what_I_claimed: MEAS-GOAL-AES-002-004 reported influence-support density 0.4996 at r=3 and read it as the object being 'dead at round 3', closing the key-indexed class.
CORRECTION_1_my_own_influence_probe_had_.red_team_finding_F2: The density statistic has NO POWER by construction: any function with balanced output bits has expected density exactly 1/2, so 0.4996 could not have come out otherwise past round 2. A controlled null was read as a closure.
CORRECTION_1_my_own_influence_probe_had_.I_VERIFIED_THIS_AND_IT_IS_CORRECT: A PURE RANDOM FUNCTION with zero structure measures 0.4995 on my own probe, against my AES reading of 0.4996. The statistic cannot distinguish structured from structureless; it detects only incomplete diffusion at r=1,2.
CORRECTION_1_my_own_influence_probe_had_.the_statistic_with_power: Per-cell BIAS, which the red team measured at +43.84 sd from null at r=3 - exactly where I reported saturation - reaching null at r=4.
CORRECTION_1_my_own_influence_probe_had_.status: MEAS-GOAL-AES-002-004's closure of the key-indexed class is WITHDRAWN as stated. The object is dead one round later than I reported, and by a different statistic. The receipt is NOT edited; this is the correction of record.
CORRECTION_1_my_own_influence_probe_had_.residual_honesty: The red team's own probe resolves to ~2^-8.8 per cell while the relevant threshold is 2^-40, so 'at the null' means 'below an instrument ~30 bits too blunt'. That applies to its probe AND to mine, with more force to mine.

CORRECTION_2_the_O3_premise_is_measurabl.O3_as_stated: Any attack enumerating candidates and paying at least one S-box per candidate is floored at 2^kappa / N_S, N_S = 200 for AES-128, giving a max class gain of 7.64 bits.
CORRECTION_2_the_O3_premise_is_measurabl.red_team_finding_F1: O-3 assumes the test is per-candidate (t=0). A procedure spending c S-boxes to eliminate a structured set of 2^t candidates pays c/2^t each. Nothing in O-3 or its supporting derivations bounds t. Pass 1 disposed of this in one sentence, which is an assertion rather than a derivation, and it is the whole closure.

I_MEASURED_IT.quantity: mu = distinct S-box computations required for an entire structured key set, divided by set size. O-3 assumes mu >= 1.
I_MEASURED_IT.method: Affine cosets of the AES-128 master key, dimension d, fixed plaintext; count distinct S-box INPUT bytes at each of the 200 positions across the whole coset; sum and divide by 2^d. Own AES-128 implementation with all 200 S-box inputs instrumented.
I_MEASURED_IT.pre_registered_discriminator: mu must RISE toward 1 as d grows if O-3's premise holds.
I_MEASURED_IT.outcome: mu FALLS: 194 -> 125 -> 12.3. The discriminator fired in the direction that contradicts the premise.
I_MEASURED_IT.analytic_bound: Distinct S-box computations over ANY key set are capped at 200 positions x 256 byte values = 51200 = 2^15.64. Therefore mu <= 2^15.64 / 2^d, which is BELOW 1 for every d > 15.64. At d=12 the measurement already reads 50432 of the 51200 cap - the coset has essentially saturated the S-box input space.
I_MEASURED_IT.conclusion: O-3's premise 'at least one S-box per candidate' is FALSE for structured key sets of dimension above about 16. Per-candidate S-box work is not bounded below by 1; it tends to zero as the set grows.

CORRECTION_2_the_O3_premise_is_measurabl.WHAT_THIS_DOES_NOT_SHOW_AND_IT_IS_THE_WH: It does NOT show that a full candidate TEST costs less than one AES evaluation. The linear-layer and XOR work is still incurred per candidate and does not amortize the way the S-box table does. O-3 counted S-boxes as a PROXY for total work; the proxy is now measurably broken, but no attack follows from that. The open question is whether the non-S-box work also amortizes over a structured set.
CORRECTION_2_the_O3_premise_is_measurabl.status: The 7.64-bit ceiling is NOT withdrawn as an arithmetic statement about S-box counts, but its status as a bound on ATTACK COST is downgraded to unproven. Every claim in this campaign that the enumerative class 'cannot move an exponent by construction' rested on it and is correspondingly weakened.

other_red_team_findings_recorded.F3: One property was promoted to a class: depth_wall_receipt correctly says it measured ONE property, then influence_support_receipt cites it as closing 'the structural classes' plural. Also depth_wall_summary used two untagged recalled figures to DISMISS, which is the symmetric-prohibition half of the rules, forgotten. Also a real C bug in integral_depth_probe.c line 42 (argv[2] cast as ternary condition, atoi/strtoull with no stdlib.h) - printed seed right only by accident, accumulators unaffected.
other_red_team_findings_recorded.F4: The S-box equation count was DERIVED exactly rather than recalled: 39 independent quadratics from 137 monomials at rank 98, so M = 200 x 39 = 7800 is now measured. Null control never run before: a random 8-bit bijection satisfies ZERO quadratics. Attacker-favourable attack on semi-regularity: each generator has rank <= 16 of N=1408 and the quadratic generators are variable-disjoint across 200 blocks with all coupling linear.
other_red_team_findings_recorded.F5: The key schedule as a standalone object was never treated and DOES NOT SATURATE: AES-128 master-bit to round-key-bit support saturates at exactly 25/32 = 0.78125 and never reaches 1, verified against the CPU's own aeskeygenassist with 0 mismatches over 200000 keys. This falsifies the diffusion reasoning the MITM argument rested on, though that argument survives on the simpler ground that round key 0 IS the master key. The red team also reported that its OWN symbolic closure said 1.0 at round 5 and is wrong because OR-based closure cannot represent XOR cancellation.
other_red_team_findings_recorded.F6: It built a second property, got r=5 z=7.61, and KILLED IT ITSELF after computing the degeneracy exactly and finding the residual excess equally present in the matched null at every round 4-10.
other_red_team_findings_recorded.F7: Classes neither pass considered: TMTO (zero mentions), slide (zero), weak keys (only as a sampling caveat). All adjudicated as not beating exhaustive search with everything charged.

net_effect_on_the_campaign_conclusion: No break is found and none is claimed. But two of the five closures are now weaker than stated: the key-indexed closure is withdrawn as stated and re-established one round later by a different statistic, and the enumerative ceiling's status as a bound on attack cost is downgraded to unproven. The honest position is that the enumerative lane has an OPEN question - whether non-S-box work amortizes over a structured key set - which no measurement here has closed.
not_established: No claim about AES security. No impossibility claim. Nothing here is a break, and the O-3 finding is a defect in an argument rather than progress toward an attack.
The mu measurement covers affine master-key cosets only, at d <= 12 measured plus an analytic cap. Other structured families are unmeasured.
Coordinator-side; the red team and both ideation passes and this session all share one model under 0137a051, so none of this is model-independent review.
